draft.title: Personal and business tax
card: Income tax
Income tax is charged on taxable income in steps called tax brackets. Each bracket has its own rate, and only the income inside a bracket is taxed at that rate.
Medicare levy
The Medicare levy is a set percentage of taxable income that helps pay for public health care. It is paid on top of income tax.
Super and rates
Superannuation is money an employer pays into a worker's retirement fund. Council rates are a yearly charge paid by property owners to their local council.
Company tax
Companies pay company tax as a percentage of their profit. Example: a 2% levy on taxable income of $50 000 is 0.02 × 50 000 = $1000.
draft.remember: Tax is worked out on taxable income, bracket by bracket, and the levy is added on top.

a.q: Ben has taxable income of $40 000. The Medicare levy is 2%. How much levy does he pay?
a.why: Levy = 2% × 40 000 = 0.02 × 40 000 = $800. $80 comes from moving the decimal point one place too far.
a.clue: Change 2% to a decimal, then multiply by taxable income.

b.q: A tax scale taxes the first $18 000 at 0% and every dollar above that at 20%. Priya's taxable income is $30 000. How much income tax does she pay?
b.why: Only the income above $18 000 is taxed at 20%. That is 30 000 − 18 000 = $12 000, and 0.2 × 12 000 = $2400. $6000 is wrong because it taxes all $30 000 at 20%.
b.clue: Only the income inside the 20% bracket is taxed at 20%.
